subject: Basic Mechanical Engineering

questions.markdown: Equal quantity of steam is supplied to a mixing chamber from two boilers through two pipe connections. One boiler supplies steam which is 87% dry and the other boiler supplies superheated steam at $325^\circ\text{C}$. The steam pressure in both the boilers and in the mixing chamber is 15 bar. Determine the quality and temperature of the steam in the mixing chamber. Assume the specific heat of superheated steam as $2.25\,\text{kJ/kg K}$.

Briefly explain the functions of the following:

a) Fusible Plug  b) Steam Trap  c) Economizer  d) Feed Check Valve  e) Air Preheater

Determine the power transmitted from an open belt running over two pulleys 1.5m and 1.0m diameter that connects two parallel shafts 5m apart. The initial tension in the belt when it is stationary is 3000N. The smaller pulley is rotating at 750 rpm and coefficient of friction between the belt and pulley is 0.25.

There are 5 wheels having 20, 30, 40, 50 and 90 teeth with a diametrical pitch of 3 and another set of 4 wheels of diametrical pitch of 2 having 20, 40, 60 and 80 teeth. Sketch an arrangement to get maximum velocity ratio using maximum number of wheels from the above lot. Calculate the velocity ratio and list the criteria to meet the above said requirements.
Differentiate a simple gear train from a compound gear train by listing 6 points each.

From a test on a four stroke petrol engine, the following data is available: engine speed 2000 rpm, net brake torque 140 N-m, indicative mean effective pressure 2MPa, stroke 15 cm, bore 10 cm, rate of fuel consumption 10.28 kg/hr, CV of petrol 41000 kJ/kg. Calculate the indicated thermal efficiency, brake thermal efficiency and mechanical efficiency.
With neat sketches and illustrating the pressure volume changes explain the working of a 4 stroke diesel engine.
Explain with a simple sketch, taper turning operation by swiveling the compound rest.

Discuss the functions of the following parts of a Lathe machine.

i) Headstock

ii) Tailstock

iii) Bed
Sketch and explain the principle of operation of a radial drilling machine.

Discuss the significance of the below listed properties of a moulding sand.

i) Permeability

ii) Adhesiveness

iii) Collapsibility

iv) Refractoriness

Explain the following operations that can be carried out on a drilling machine:

i) Reaming

ii) Boring

iii) Spot facing
Explain with a simple sketch, the working principle of resistance spot welding.
